$comment: Where each operation of pydiggs.capabilities() stands in @pydiggs/client. Every operation id is listed in exactly one section; tests/test_js_client_coverage.py fails when pyDIGGS gains an operation that is not, so a new pyDIGGS feature is a decision for the client in the pull request that adds it. js/test/coverage.test.ts holds the 'offered' methods to the code. 'hybrid' is true when PydiggsHybrid offers the methods too (operations on a document). A 'planned' entry names the methods it will add and why; once they exist on every engine, js/test/coverage.test.ts fails until the entry moves to 'offered'.

tables.to-diggs.why: The HTTP API (POST /v1/tables/*) and the sidecar (tables.* methods, protocol 1.4) offer it since this release; the client methods come in a later release, on every engine at once (HTTP, the Pyodide worker, the pool and the hybrid client) with createPydiggsHandler routes, generated result types and tests, as convert and diff came. Until then, call the HTTP API or the sidecar directly.

not_offered.detect: No HTTP route; validate and read detect the DIGGS version themselves and report it.
not_offered.ags4.read: Returns Python AGS4 tables; in JavaScript, convert an AGS4 file to DIGGS and read that.
not_offered.ags4.write: Writes Python AGS4 tables; in JavaScript, convert with to: "ags4".
not_offered.gis.transform: Needs the gis extra (pyproj), which the Pyodide engine does not install.
not_offered.export.geodataframe: A Python GeoDataFrame; needs the gis extra.
not_offered.export.gpkg: Needs the gis extra (pyogrio), which the Pyodide engine does not install.
not_offered.export.geoparquet: Needs the gis extra (pyarrow), which the Pyodide engine does not install.
not_offered.export.geojson: Needs the gis extra (pyogrio), which the Pyodide engine does not install.
not_offered.write: Writes a Python model; no HTTP route or sidecar method takes a model. Writing DIGGS from tables is tables.to-diggs.
